speaker: Doctor
text: Since both your brain and cervical spine MRIs are normal, I need to rule out peripheral nerve or metabolic causes. Can you tell me if you experience any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your hands or feet, and do you have any history of diabetes or alcohol use? Also, have you noticed any changes in your vision or hearing?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the normal MRIs and your description of unilateral clumsiness, could you tell me if your symptoms worsen significantly when you walk in the dark or if you have any difficulty distinguishing between similar colors? Additionally, do you have any history of diabetes, thyroid issues, or recent infections like the flu?

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since your metabolic workup and imaging are normal, I need to narrow down if this is a spinocerebellar degeneration or a paraneoplastic syndrome. Have you noticed any recent weight loss, fever, or swollen lymph nodes, and have you ever had a testicular lump or skin changes?

REQUEST TEST: CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis
REQUEST TEST: Paraneoplastic Panel (Anti-Yo, Anti-Hu)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis: No masses, lymphadenopathy, or abnormalities detected. Paraneoplastic Panel (Anti-Yo, Anti-Hu): Negative.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal metabolic, imaging, and tumor screens, this points strongly toward a hereditary spinocerebellar ataxia. Can you describe any other neurological signs like tremors, muscle stiffness, or jerky movements? Additionally, do you have any known family members with similar walking difficulties or vision problems? Finally, have you noticed any changes in your handwriting or difficulty buttoning your shirt?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced Cerebellar Ataxia secondary to Natalizumab therapy. Given your history of Crohn's disease and the temporal onset of ataxia after one year of treatment, this is highly suggestive of a paraneoplastic-like reaction or immune-mediated cerebellar degeneration associated with Natalizumab. We should discontinue the medication immediately and consider a repeat MRI of the brain to assess for any new cerebellar changes.
